SPEC-OBJECT.ATTR: As a clinician, I need the injector's needle interface to minimize risk of needle-stick injury and misinsertion during contrast administration.
As a clinician, I need a secure, leak-free connection between the injector syringe and the patient catheter line.
As a clinician, I need the injector to deliver contrast at a precisely controlled, programmable flow rate and volume.
As a clinician, I need the system to prevent injection of air into the patient's vasculature.
As a clinician, I need reliable tracking of contrast media inventory and expiration status in the reservoir/syringe.
As a clinician, I need the system to detect line occlusion before it causes patient injury or extravasation.
As a clinician, I need alarms that reliably reach my attention with appropriate priority and are distinguishable from one another.
As a clinician, I need a programming interface that prevents entry of clinically unsafe injection parameters.
As a clinician, I need the injector to keep operating safely through a mains power interruption during an injection.
As a clinician and biomed engineer, I need a complete, tamper-evident record of every injection delivered for the patient record and audits.
As a biomed and infection-control engineer, I need reusable components to be validated for the facility's reprocessing procedure between patients.
As a biomed engineer, I need the injector head and console to survive the mechanical and environmental conditions of a busy imaging suite.
As a systems engineer, I need an independent software safety monitor that catches a runaway or hung main control loop before it can harm the patient.
As a biomed and IT engineer, I need the injector's network connection to the EMR/RIS to be secure and to never block a needed injection.
The system shall support single-use needles with gauge sizes from 18G to 24G for peripheral IV access.
The injector shall reject a programmed flow rate that exceeds the maximum rate rated for the detected needle gauge.
The system shall provide a passive needle-shielding mechanism that engages automatically upon withdrawal.
The needle-shielding mechanism shall present a visible indicator confirming it has engaged before the needle is discarded.
The system shall display the compatible needle gauge range on the injector head housing.
The compatible needle gauge label shall be provided in English and at least one additional facility-configurable language.
The syringe-to-catheter connector shall be a standard luer-lock fitting rated to withstand injection pressures up to 325 psi without disconnection.
The system shall provide a visible or tactile confirmation that the luer-lock connection is fully seated before permitting injection.
The system shall detect a pressure drop consistent with a line disconnect or leak within 2 seconds of onset and halt injection.
The leak-detection alarm shall annunciate within 500 ms of leak detection.
The pressure sensor used for leak detection shall execute a zero-offset self-check before each injection.
The system shall restrict programmable flow rate and pressure limits to values compatible with the catheter gauge selected by the operator.
An operator override of the catheter compatibility restriction shall require a two-step confirmation and shall be logged.
The injector shall deliver programmed flow rate within +/-5% of setpoint across the rated range of 0.1 to 10 mL/s.
The pump control loop shall sample the flow sensor at 100 Hz and adjust motor drive within one control cycle.
The injector shall support a field flow-rate calibration procedure traceable to a certified reference volume.
The injector shall deliver the programmed total volume within +/-2% for volumes between 5 and 200 mL.
The system shall support a field volume-accuracy verification procedure using a calibrated graduated cylinder.
For dual-syringe (contrast/saline) configurations, the system shall synchronize switchover to within 50 ms of the programmed transition point.
The system shall support programmable contrast:saline mixing ratios from 100:0 to 0:100 in 10% increments.
The injector shall enforce an operator-programmable maximum line pressure limit between 50 and 325 psi.
The enforced maximum pressure limit shall automatically derate by 20% when ambient temperature exceeds 30 C, per the pump's thermal rating.
The system shall detect an air column of 0.10 mL or greater in the fluid path using ultrasonic air-in-line sensing.
Upon air detection, the system shall halt the pump motor within 100 ms.
The air-in-line sensor shall execute a power-on self-test and fault to a safe state if the self-test fails.
The system shall provide a guided air-purge priming sequence before the line is connected to the patient.
Completion of the air-purge sequence shall be verified by the air-in-line sensor reading clear before the system enables patient connection.
The system shall annunciate a distinct audible and visual alarm pattern specific to air-in-line detection, distinguishable from occlusion alarms.
The system shall continuously monitor contrast reservoir fill level and estimate remaining deliverable volume within +/-3 mL.
The system shall issue a low-reservoir warning when remaining volume falls below the volume required to complete the programmed protocol.
The system shall record the contrast lot number and expiration date scanned at syringe load and block injection past the expiration date.
The system shall warn, but not block, injection of contrast within 24 hours of its expiration date, and shall block outright after expiration.
The system shall verify contrast concentration and volume against a scanned barcode before enabling injection.
A barcode scan that does not match the previously loaded lot shall require operator re-confirmation before proceeding.
The system shall detect a line occlusion when measured pressure exceeds the operator-set occlusion threshold for more than 300 ms.
The occlusion pressure threshold shall be programmable from 10 to 300 psi in 5 psi increments.
Upon occlusion detection, the pump shall halt motor drive within 200 ms and hold the last commanded position.
The system shall flag a suspected extravasation pattern when pressure rises gradually without reaching the hard occlusion threshold, using a slope-based heuristic.
A suspected extravasation pattern shall present a distinct on-screen advisory recommending clinical assessment, separate from the hard occlusion alarm.
Occlusion alarms shall be assigned the highest annunciation priority level in the alarm system, per IEC 60601-1-8 style prioritization.
The system shall implement three alarm priority levels (high, medium, low) each with a distinct audible pattern per IEC 60601-1-8.
Each alarm priority level shall be paired with a distinct visual indicator color (red, yellow, cyan).
An operator-initiated alarm silence shall time out and re-annunciate after no more than 120 seconds if the underlying condition persists.
The maximum single silence duration for a high-priority alarm shall not exceed 2 minutes, per IEC 60601-1-8.
The system shall retain the most recent 500 alarm events in non-volatile storage with timestamp and acknowledgment record.
The system shall support exporting the alarm log in a structured, human-readable format for service review.
The user interface shall reject entry of a flow rate, volume, or pressure limit outside the clinically validated range for the selected protocol.
The user interface shall require a second, explicit confirmation before accepting a programmed parameter that exceeds a soft warning threshold.
The system shall provide a library of at least 10 preconfigured injection protocols selectable by exam type.
The system shall allow a site administrator to add up to 20 custom protocols to the library, subject to the same range validation as built-in protocols.
The user interface shall lock out parameter entry while the system reports an active cleaning or reprocessing cycle.
A supervisor override of the cleaning-cycle lockout shall require a service PIN and shall be logged.
The system shall provide battery backup capable of completing an in-progress injection and safely parking the pump for at least 5 minutes after loss of mains power.
The system shall monitor battery state of health and issue a service alert when capacity falls below 80% of rated.
Upon mains power loss, the system shall preserve the in-progress protocol state and resume without requiring re-programming once power is restored.
The system shall detect a ground fault condition on the patient-connected circuit and disconnect within the time limits of IEC 60601-1.
Ground fault protection circuitry shall be exercised by a self-test at power-on.
The system shall record programmed and actually-delivered flow rate, volume, and pressure profile for every injection.
Each injection record shall include a checksum to detect post-hoc tampering.
The system shall support exporting injection records in a structured format for integration with the hospital information system.
The system shall log operator identity and timestamp for every parameter change, in a separate append-only audit trail.
The audit trail shall retain at least 2 years of operator action records before the oldest records may be archived.
The system shall synchronize its internal clock to facility network time within +/-1 second when connected to the network.
If network time is unavailable, the system shall fall back to its internal real-time clock and flag records with a reduced-confidence timestamp source.
Reusable fluid-path components shall be validated to withstand the facility's specified high-level disinfection cycle for a minimum of 100 cycles.
The system shall display the remaining validated reprocessing cycle count for a reusable component that reports a use-counter.
The system shall detect an already-used single-use syringe or tubing set, via an embedded use-counter chip, and prevent reuse.
An override of the single-use lockout shall require a documented service-level authorization code, logged in the audit trail.
External housing materials shall be compatible with the facility's list of approved surface disinfectants without degradation over 500 wipe cycles.
The injector head shall meet at least IP34 fluid-ingress protection to tolerate incidental contrast spillage.
The system shall meet IEC 60601-1-2 electromagnetic immunity requirements for use adjacent to CT and angiography equipment.
If offered in an MRI-conditional configuration, the system shall be labeled per ASTM F2503 MRI conditional labeling requirements.
The mobile console shall withstand a 75 cm drop onto a hard floor on any face without loss of basic safety function.
The mobile console shall not tip over when the loaded injector head arm is extended to its maximum reach at any caster-locked orientation.
The system shall provide a visible indicator of caster-lock engagement state.
An independent hardware watchdog timer shall force a safe-state stop if the main control loop fails to service it within 250 ms.
The watchdog circuit shall be exercised as part of power-on self-test before the system is placed in a ready state.
Line pressure shall be independently measured by two physically separate sensors, and injection shall halt if the two readings disagree by more than 15%.
The system shall verify a cryptographic signature on the control software image at boot and refuse to run an unsigned or modified image.
A failed software update shall automatically roll back to the last known-good verified image.
Following any detected fault, the system shall enter a defined safe state, motor de-energized, valve closed, alarm active, within 500 ms.
Loss of network connectivity to the EMR/RIS shall not prevent the system from delivering a locally-programmed injection.
Patient worklist data received from the EMR shall be validated, patient ID and exam type, against the operator's manual entry before an injection is enabled.
Data exchanged with the EMR/RIS over the network shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
Remote service access to the injector's diagnostic interface shall require multi-factor authentication and shall be logged.
A remote service session shall automatically terminate after 15 minutes of inactivity.
